The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

messages.content: Please keep it simple and just name the bad part. This is my 2019 midsize sedan. It has the 2.5-liter four, the automatic transmission and about 100,266 miles. reply: Measure front rotor lateral runout: with the hub face cleaned and the lug nuts torqued to spec, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with its plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and turn the rotor one full revolution [TSB-0529]. snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that soften as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans, small crossovers and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Misfire while idle from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire while idle may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) may set with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition

Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor, model years 2016-2021. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2017 compact sedan, 2.0L, automatic transmission, odometer 101,062. P0171 keeps coming back a day after I clear it. The idle shakes the steering wheel a bit when it's cold, and the freeze frame says it set at idle. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?
Begin here: with the engine idling, inspect the PCV hose where it joins the intake elbow, flexing it gently while you listen for a vacuum hiss [SM-6321].
My buddy says skip the tests and get a mass airflow sensor. Thoughts?
A part guess could cost you twice. With the engine idling, inspect the PCV hose where it joins the intake elbow, flexing it gently while you listen for a vacuum hiss [SM-6321].
Grudgingly did the test. I flexed the PCV hose at the elbow with it idling. No cracks and no hiss.

That result clears it. With the engine off, smoke-test the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke [SM 2.8.7].
The smoke test was clean, nothing leaking at the manifold, throttle body or hoses. Okay, so what's the follow-up check?

reply: A clean smoke test rules out unmetered air, so check fuel delivery: with the key on and engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the fuel rail test port on your 2.0L and look for 55-62 psi, holding within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off [B-21-208].

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) may set with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

reply: Start with an AC operating pressure check on your 3.5L V6: connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports, hold the engine at 1,500 rpm with the AC at maximum and the doors open, and compare both readings with the chart for today's ambient temperature [SM 7.3.3]. Around 80 deg F, expect roughly 25-45 psi low side and 150-250 psi high side, and wear eye protection at the ports.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines, model years 2010-2022. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side. Wear eye protection at the ports.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2016-2021. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link. A short pry bar helps on stiff links.

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan, model years 2009-2021. Vent air may blow warm when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: On 2016-2021 models, with the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

reply: Have a helper bounce the front of your crossover firmly while you rest a hand on the left strut upper mount under the hood, feeling for a knock each time the suspension compresses [SM-2429]. A distinct knock felt right at that mount would match the low-speed clunk over bumps that you're hearing on the left.

snippets.title: Front clunk when turning slowly from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk only while you are turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat overnight in freezing air even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.

reply: Hook a pressure gauge to the transmission's line pressure test port with the engine fully warm, where your hard shifts show up, and check the reading while idling in drive with the brake applied: it should sit between 55 and 75 psi and climb smoothly as you add throttle [SEC 14.23]. A reading above that range would point to line pressure being held too high once the fluid heats up.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that worsen as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2015 compact sedan, 2.0L, automatic transmission, 83k miles logged. Hard, delayed shifts once the car is warm. The first few miles cold are actually smoother. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

reply: Since the shifts get harsher once it's warm and smoother cold, start by connecting a pressure gauge to the transmission's line pressure test port with the fluid at operating temperature. Idle in drive with the brake firmly applied and confirm you see 55-75 psi, rising with throttle; a reading held above that range points to excessive line pressure [SEC 14.23].

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Misfire while idle from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire while idle may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

messages.content: Our family's 2016 hatchback with the 1.6L four-cylinder and the stick shift, just past 65k miles. Misfire code P0304. reply: Clean the rust scale off the measuring track on each front rotor and use an outside micrometer to measure thickness at eight evenly spaced points about half an inch in from the outer edge, looking for variation above 0.0005 in, which would explain pedal pulsation when slowing from highway speed [SM-8904]. I know you're ready to order something, but your 0.001 in runout is within spec, and this measurement narrows it down without guessing.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes and an automatic transmission. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes, model years 2010-2015. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed. Clean rust scale off the measuring track first.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the steering wheel may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2015 full-size pickup, 5.5-liter V8, automatic transmission, odometer 170,743. The battery keeps going flat over a long weekend. Once it's jumped it starts every day as long as I drive it daily. No warning lights while driving, and it isn't cold out. The dealer wants a diagnostic fee I can't afford. Which part is it?

reply: I understand the dealer fee is a hard pill. Instead of guessing at a part, here's a check you can do yourself with a basic voltmeter. After a 20-minute drive, hold the engine at 2,000 rpm with the headlights and blower on and measure voltage right at the battery posts, not the cable clamps, where 13.5–14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery [SM 1.4.6].

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs, minivans and compact crossovers. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after several days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.

reply: With the car parked and the engine off, have a helper bounce the front left corner while you rest a hand on the strut's upper mount under the hood, feeling for a knock that matches the clunk you hear over speed bumps [SM-2460]. On a 2017 sedan with front struts, a distinct knock you can feel right at that mount points the diagnosis there.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk over bumps or when turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.

messages.content: Hi. 2017 midsize sedan, 3.5L V6 engine, automatic, roughly 150k on the odometer. There's a clunk from the front left when I go over speed bumps or potholes at low speed, driving straight. Nothing when I turn the wheel in a parking lot. One more thing: I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm.

reply: Thanks for the detail on that front-left clunk over bumps. With a helper bouncing the front of the car, rest your hand on the left strut's upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock coming through it each time the suspension compresses, since a worn upper mount or bearing on strut-equipped cars from these years can clunk exactly like that over bumps [SM-2460].

reply: Hook a pressure gauge to the transmission's line pressure test port and, with the fluid fully warm and the engine idling in drive with the brake applied, read the line pressure, which should sit between 55 and 75 psi and rise as you add throttle [SM-5282]. Testing it hot matters because your SUV's shifts get harsher as the fluid warms.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that soften as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2016-2021. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2011-2021. With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 5.5L V8 engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

Good details, thanks. The first check is this: with the transmission at operating temperature and the engine idling in park on level ground, check the fluid level against the hot range and look at its color and smell [SEC 2.4].
Level is right in the hot range and the fluid looks clean.
Normal there. With the brake held firmly, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine for lift or a gap at any mount [SB 59-983].
No real lift at all going between drive and reverse. So what do you want me to test now?

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Hi. 2017 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6 engine, automatic transmission, roughly 100,997 on the odometer. Misfire code P0304. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. How would you approach this first?

Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [TSB-9226]. Let me know what you find.
Hooked up a spark tester at 25 kV. Strong blue spark every time.

Thanks for checking. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [SM 5.3.4].
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain. I'm about done with checks. Is it time to buy the part?

snippets.title: Dim lights in cold snaps from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim only in cold snaps when a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.

snippets.title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

reply: With the engine idling, preferably from a cold start, look closely at the underside of the PCV hose where it joins the intake elbow, and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss [SEC 12.6]. On your 2.5L, a hiss or a visible crack there would mean unmetered air is getting in, which fits a P0171 with an idle that hunts mostly while the engine is cold.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor, model years 2016-2021. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the front seatback may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) may set with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

reply: Measure the parked current draw on your 2017 SUV with an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal, with the hood switch latched, all doors closed and up to 45 minutes allowed for the modules to go to sleep; the reading should settle below 50 mA [TSB-0716]. A draw that stays above that would explain a battery that charges fine while driving but goes flat after a few days in the airport lot.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester

A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: On 2016-2021 models, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side. Probe the terminals themselves, not the cable clamps, so a loose clamp shows up.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test

A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Misfire while idle from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire while idle may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

reply: Set your meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts with the 2.4-liter running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on. Ripple should stay below 0.5 V AC, and a higher reading points to a rectifier diode problem that would explain the dim lights and the battery light at idle [SM-5224].

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the steering wheel may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that worsen as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

reply: Hook a pressure gauge to the transmission's line pressure test port and, with the engine idling in drive and your foot firmly on the brake, you should see 55-75 psi that climbs as you add throttle [SB 72-561]. snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

I'd hold off on buying the O2 sensor, because low fuel pressure alone can set a lean code like your P0171 and cause that rough idle, and this reading settles it with a measurement.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the front seatback may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation

reply: Get the fluid fully warmed up, park the SUV on level ground and leave it idling in park, then check the automatic transmission fluid level against the hot range and look at its condition. It should be red or pink with no burnt smell or debris, since low or degraded fluid causes exactly the delayed engagement and harsh shifts you're describing [SB 80-072].

snippets.title: CVT fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a continuously-variable (CVT) gearbox, model years 2011-2021. With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2011-2021. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2015. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts with a digital meter. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output. Clean any corrosion from the posts first so it does not skew the reading.

The idle is rough, worst for the first few minutes after a cold start. And while I'm at it, hard, delayed shifts once the car is warm. The first few miles cold are actually smoother.

reply: Start with a cold-engine pressure test: fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir on your 2.5L, pump it to the pressure stamped on the cap, and confirm it holds for 15 minutes while you look for seepage at the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks [SEC 14.11]. A slow loss like yours often leaves no puddle.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

A reading that has dropped below that means rail pressure is bleeding down and letting fuel boil in the hot rail, which matches the long crank you're getting after a short stop.

snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2015. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later. It should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the pump module.

snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 3.4L V6 and 5.5L V8 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2010-2015. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link. A short pry bar helps on stiff links.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Scale or debris in the radiator core can make temperature climb at idle and in traffic. With the engine warm and the thermostat open, compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank using an infrared thermometer. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: flush or replace the radiator.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines, model years 2010-2022. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor

Repair: clean the sensor element or replace the sensor.

A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

reply: Measure the parasitic draw on your 2017 sedan with an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal, with the hood switch latched and the doors closed so the modules can go to sleep [SM 3.3.3]. snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans, small crossovers and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake

Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

messages.content: The front left side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. Daily driver is a 2015 compact sedan (2.0-liter four, auto trans) with 160k miles. Any idea which check to begin with?

reply: A knock over small bumps on a 2015 sedan with 160k is worth chasing at the front left. With the car sitting on its wheels so the suspension is loaded, grab the front stabilizer link and push and pull it firmly while watching both ball studs; any free play, a knock you can feel, or a torn boot leaking grease means the link is worn [TSB-0339].

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2015. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts with a digital meter. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output. Clean any corrosion from the posts first so it does not skew the reading.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Overheating at speed from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Scale or debris in the radiator core can make temperature climb at speed and on grades. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: flush or replace the radiator.

snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire while idle may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Dim lights in cold snaps from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim only in cold snaps when a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2019 midsize SUV (3.4L V6, automatic transmission) with 113,548 miles. Shimmy in the steering wheel only when braking from 60 mph or so. Light stops around town on smooth roads are fine. How would you approach this first?

reply: With the lug nuts torqued to spec and the hub face clean, mount a dial indicator to the front knuckle with the plunger about half an inch in from the rotor's outer edge and turn the rotor one full revolution [SB 54-861]. Steering-wheel pulsation under braking from highway speed on your minivan fits high lateral runout, and the reading shouldn't exceed 0.002 inch.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Never open the cap on a hot engine. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the steering wheel may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor, model years 2010-2015. Lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle may set when a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine warm and idling and all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement. Do not touch the sensor element. Repair: clean the sensor element or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that worsen as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side. Wear eye protection at the ports.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, minivans and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after several days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2015. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2018 minivan (3.5L V6, automatic) with 175,945 miles. The battery keeps going flat over a long weekend. Once it's jumped it starts every day as long as I drive it daily. No warning lights while driving, and it isn't cold out. What test makes sense right now?
Good details, thanks. The first check is this: fully charge the battery, let it rest, and run a conductance or load test against the CCA rating on its label [SB 12-635].

reply: With the engine cold, take the pressure cap off your 2014 crossover, fit it to a pressure tester adapter and pump until it vents; it should hold at least the rating stamped on the cap [TSB-5998]. A cap that vents early can let coolant escape through the overflow as vapor, which fits slow loss with no drips or steam, so this test is worth doing before spending on a radiator.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes and a manual-clutch transaxle. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans and hatchbacks. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

snippets.title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. Coolant may drop slowly with no visible leak when the pressure cap vents early and coolant escapes through the overflow as vapor. Fit the cap to a pressure tester adapter and pump until it vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2010-2015. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. reply: Measure front rotor lateral runout: with the lug nuts torqued to spec and the hub face cleaned, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge, rotate the rotor one full turn, and expect no more than 0.002 in [B-11-198]. Pulsation through the steering wheel when braking from highway speed is the pattern this check targets.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the front seatback may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes, model years 2016-2021. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed. Clean rust scale off the measuring track first.

With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

A tester with a squeeze bulb makes the draw easier.

snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts with a digital meter. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output. Clean any corrosion from the posts first so it does not skew the reading.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: On 2010-2015 models, with the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2015. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later. It should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the pump module.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that worsen as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans, small crossovers and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2015. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

reply: Start with an intake smoke test on your 2016 2.0L: with the engine off, feed smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke [SM 5.3.4]. Any smoke that appears marks where unmetered air is getting in after the airflow sensor, a common source of a bank 1 lean code like your P0171.

reply: Clean fluid sitting in the hot range rules that check out, and the references I have left don't cover harsh, delayed shifts that get worse the longer you drive, so I can't point you to a further test from them. Does a scan tool show any stored transmission trouble codes?

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that soften as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2016-2021. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2011-2021. With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2017 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6, automatic, odometer 92,490. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. What test makes sense right now?
With the brake held firmly, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine for lift or a gap at any mount [SEC 10.28]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Checked it. No real lift at all going between drive and reverse.

That result clears it. With the transmission at operating temperature and the engine idling in park on level ground, check the fluid level against the hot range and look at its color and smell [SEC 5.13].
Level is right in the hot range and the fluid looks clean. Which test makes sense now that this one came back fine?

reply: With the 2.5L fully warmed up and idling, all accessories off, read the MAF airflow on a scan tool and compare it with roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement, about 2.5 g/s for your engine [SM 3.6.4]. snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor, model years 2010-2015. Lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle may set when a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine warm and idling and all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement. Do not touch the sensor element. Repair: clean the sensor element or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) may set with a rough idle that is worst on a warm engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

snippets.title: Long crank on cold starts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on cold starts. On any cold start, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the front seatback may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

reply: Run a cranking compression test with fuel and ignition disabled and all spark plugs out, cranking each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open, and expect all six to read within 10 percent of each other [TSB-0583]. Since spark and the plug both checked out on your 2017 V6, a low reading on cylinder 2 would point to a mechanical cause rather than ignition or fuel.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

messages.content: Mine is a midsize sedan from 2017, 3.5-liter V6 under the hood, automatic transmission, 100k miles so far. Misfire code P0302. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. Can you point me to a good starting check?

Good details, thanks. The first check is this: connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SM-7118].
My buddy says skip the tests and get a fuel injector. Thoughts?

Ordering parts without a test risks money on the wrong one. Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SM-7118].
Okay, you talked me into it, and here's what I got. The spark tester showed a solid blue spark the whole time I cranked it.

Normal there. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [SM 1.9.8].
Pulled the plug. Gap is 0.042, no cracks, and it looks like the others. Where should I go with this from here?

snippets.title: Front clunk when turning slowly from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk only while you are turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans and hatchbacks. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs, minivans and compact crossovers. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

messages.content: Mine is a full-size pickup from 2020, 5.5L V8 under the hood, automatic transmission, 85k miles so far. The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans, small crossovers and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts with a digital meter. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output. Clean any corrosion from the posts first so it does not skew the reading.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side. Wear eye protection at the ports.

reply: Run an intake smoke test with the engine off, feeding smoke in through the brake booster vacuum line and watching the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for any escaping smoke [SM-6577]. Your P0171 with a rough idle but a strong highway pull fits unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor, which is exactly what this test on your 2021 1.4L turbo is meant to reveal.

A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

reply: With the engine fully warm and the thermostat open, aim an infrared thermometer at the radiator's inlet tank and outlet tank and compare the two readings, which should normally differ by about 20-40 deg F [SB 75-716]. On your 3.5-liter V6, a much smaller difference, or cold spots as you scan across the core, would show restricted coolant flow that matches heat building at idle and easing at highway speed.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes and a manual-clutch transaxle. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Scale or debris in the radiator core can make temperature climb at idle and in traffic. With the engine warm and the thermostat open, compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank using an infrared thermometer. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: flush or replace the radiator.

reply: Measure parasitic draw with an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal, with the hood switch latched, the doors closed and up to 45 minutes allowed for the modules to sleep; the reading should settle below 50 mA [B-13-064]. Charging and battery health both checked out on your 2016 sedan, so a circuit staying awake while it sits at the airport lot is what this measurement looks for.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after several days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, minivans and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

A tester with a squeeze bulb makes the draw easier.

While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: On 2010-2015 models, with the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself, and use fresh fluid for each test. A tester with a squeeze bulb makes the draw easier.

snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 5.5L V8 engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, minivans and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes and an automatic transmission. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor, model years 2010-2015. Repair: clean the sensor element or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check

Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Overheating at speed from a restricted radiator core

snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans, small crossovers and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Mine is a minivan from 2016, 3.5-liter V6 under the hood, automatic, 180,881 miles so far. Misfire code P0302. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. Can you point me to a good starting check?

Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SEC 19.17]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Here's what I found. The spark tester showed a solid blue spark the whole time I cranked it.

Good, that clears this area. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [TSB-2357].
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain. Nothing showed up, so I'm guessing it's the ignition coil. Agree?

Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2016-2021. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. messages.content: Clunk from the front end, left side, on rough pavement. It definitely comes from the front, and it doesn't happen when turning sharply. Hi. 2013 full-size pickup, 5.5L V8 engine, automatic transmission, roughly 148k on the odometer. Which check would you run before anything else?

reply: With the engine held at 2,000 rpm and heavy loads switched on (headlights, blower on high, rear defrost), measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post and from the alternator case to the battery negative post, probing the terminals themselves rather than the cable clamps [SB 92-520]. On your 2020 crossover, the positive side should read under 0.3 V and the ground side under 0.2 V.

Never open the cap on a hot engine. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans, small crossovers and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.
